static_traits.name: Ning Ke
static_traits.family_status: Owns a small family restaurant, plans to open a bakery after retirement
static_traits.social_status: Relationship tension with friends and family; having a supportive spouse but not yet confiding inadequacy feelings to him
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; without psychotherapy history; similar problems not yet appeared in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good cooperativeness; frequently using 'should' sentences and making social comparisons; tending to negate positive feedback and focus on the negative ('negating the positive' 'mental filtering'); subjective Low mood and skepticism coexisting

basic_info.main_problem: Although I volunteer frequently at a soup kitchen, I always feel I have not done enough for the local community.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this sense of inadequacy is affecting my mood and my motivation to participate in volunteering.

core_beliefs: My contributions are not meaningful enough

special_situations.event: Sees other people organizing activities and fundraising, doing more for the community
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not done more like them, it shows I do not contribute enough / am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting higher Demands on self and self-pressure, repeatedly comparing and reflecting 'I should do more'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am only doing the minimum, I should do more to truly have an impact

special_situations.event: Almost daily when reflecting on volunteering, focusing on what she has not yet done
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my efforts have no marked and visible effect, it equals having no meaning
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly criticizes and scrutinizes my own contributions, ignoring steady investment and others' positive feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is just a small thing, not really any help at all

special_situations.event: Receives gratitude and affirmation from recipients in volunteer service
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Unless it is a 'big project / big impact', others' thanks do not represent true contribution
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proactively diluting and denying positive feedback, emphasizing inadequacy and gaps
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; this does not count

special_situations.event: When thinking about telling her spouse about her inadequacy feelings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should not trouble others, negative emotions should be digested by myself
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids communicating with and asking the spouse for help, forcing oneself to bear it alone
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not bring these things up to talk about

core_conflict.wish: Longs to produce a significant impact by helping others and be recognized as a valuable person
core_conflict.fear: Fearing she is not valuable enough, appearing inadequate compared to others
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and worth by raising self-standards and self-criticism
Avoids seeking help from the spouse to prevent exposing vulnerability
Urging self-improvement by comparing with others, relieving the Anxiety of Meaninglessness

object_relations.self_representation: An inadequate person not contributing enough, needing to do more
object_relations.object_representation: Others/groups who do more, set high standards, and implicitly judge

object_relations.self_representation: Someone who should not trouble others
object_relations.object_representation: The supportive spouse who may be burdened by my emotions

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes the positive meaning of their steady volunteer commitment or tries to restructure their self-evaluation
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing these are just 'theoretical comforts', unable to change real inadequacy (transference: treating supportive information as unrealistic)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cautious, reserved tone, emphasizing 'uncertain' 'not much use', avoiding deep emotional experience and positive meaning.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing others do more for the community or hearing of others' bigger impact
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizes others' standards as her own hard requirements (must / should)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Frequently using 'should / must' sentences, self-reproaching tone, emphasizing meeting standards and compliance.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When reflecting on volunteer Work and feeling inferior
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning outward comparisons and dissatisfaction against the self, believing it is all her own problem
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Low tone, using Self-denial words (e.g. 'I am just not enough'), reducing willingness to seek support externally.

manifestations: Volunteering regarded as 'just a small thing', hard to acknowledge its significance
Longing to make a 'marked impact', otherwise Decreased sense of self-worth
Frequently compares others' contributions with their own
outcomes: Work and everyday interests (e.g. cooking) affected

manifestations: Having a supportive spouse but choosing not to communicate her inadequacy feelings
Withdraws into herself amid self-reproach and comparison, reducing external contact and support

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Frequently using self-Demands like 'I should do more'
Treating 'significant impact' as the only valid standard

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Constantly scrutinizing and nitpicking her own contributions
In Low mood, intensifying self-criticism, reducing help-seeking

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'.
manifestations: When thanked, diluting the positive meaning, quickly turning to emphasize inadequacy
Deflecting focus with 'this is just a small thing / may not be useful' when facing the counselor's reframing attempts

exception_events.target_problem: When seeing others do more for the community or reflecting on her own contribution, the client usually compares and negates her own efforts, followed by Low mood and decreased volunteering drive.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a volunteer service, several regulars expressed thanks for the meals face to face; the client noticed the value of the stable support they provide and realized the importance of consistency and reliability to those helped.
exception_events.reason: Clues: recipients' direct thanks and concrete feedback; different understanding: incorporating the value of 'consistency and reliability' into evaluation, thus briefly seeing positive impact.

positive_force: Steadily volunteering at the soup kitchen
Willing to try setting specific goals and monitoring progress
Able to identify and name cognitive patterns (e.g. 'negating the positive' 'mental filtering')
negative_force: Negating positive feedback and focusing on inadequacy (mental filtering / negating the positive)
Low mood and decreased motivation affecting Work and daily interests
Avoiding seeking support from spouse, reinforcing inner isolation

target_behavior.behavior: When comparing others' contributions or reflecting on volunteering, producing sustained Self-denial and 'I should do more' thoughts, with Low mood and Decreased drive
antecedent: Sees others organizing activities, fundraising and doing more
Almost daily reflecting on her volunteering and its impact
target_behavior.core_reason: High expectations for 'marked impact' and rigid standards; cognitive biases like 'mental filtering' 'negating the positive' causing Impaired sense of self-worth
target_behavior.function: Maintaining moral standards and control through self-pressure and self-punishment, avoiding being seen as not valuable enough
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, decreased volunteering drive, Relationship tension with family and friends, reduced interest in daily activities (e.g. cooking)
